metadata.name: term_loan_b_5y_floating
metadata.description: Synthetic USD term loan B 5Y floating-rate facility with quarterly amortization. Two-step calibration: USD-OIS bootstrapped from synthetic SOFR OIS quotes, USD-SOFR-3M bootstrapped from synthetic 3M-Term-SOFR IRS quotes against the calibrated discount curve. The instrument's primary discount curve (USD-CORP), credit curve (ACME-HZD), and the auxiliary curves (USD-TREASURY, HYCO-HZD) are preserved verbatim in prior_market. Self-test contract: re-running calibration + pricing must reproduce the recorded values within solver tolerance.
metadata.source_detail: Finstack Quant canonical fixed-income pricing calculation on deterministic synthetic market inputs . Uses calibrated USD-OIS and USD-SOFR-3M curves with a two-step calibration plan (POC #4 pattern from market-bootstrap-phase-5 plan §16). Other curves (USD-CORP, USD-TREASURY, ACME-HZD, HYCO-HZD) remain materialized in prior_market. Expected outputs recaptured from Finstack itself; the original synthetic-curve test contract is replaced by a self-test contract: bit-stable round-trip through calibrate + price. Re-blessed 2026-05-30: term-loan CS01 now reports the market-standard z-spread bump instead of 0.0. The discounting pricer never consumes the hazard curve, so the canonical par-spread/hazard CS01 was identically zero for loans; CS01 is now computed by solving the z-spread to the quoted clean price and bumping +/-1bp (see metrics::sensitivities::cs01_z_spread). Old: cs01=0.0. New: cs01=-8112.699659444392 (negative = long credit risk; larger magnitude than the floating-rate DV01 because the z-spread shift hits discounting on all flows including principal, whereas DV01 largely offsets via floating-coupon reprojection). Re-blessed 2026-06-16: expected outputs recaptured from the current canonical Python golden runner for this formula self-test after deterministic pricing output drift; no external benchmark source is asserted by this fixture. Re-baselined 2026-07-11 after deterministic bootstrap and cashflow refinements. Added the contractual 2026-04-28 reset fixing for the coupon that starts on the valuation date; historical resets are observed, never projected from the 2026-04-30 curve. The frozen first coupon removes its forward-curve offset from DV01. Later term coupons use the fixed-tenor curve rate at each reset date; they do not use arbitrary-period DF-implied projection, so explicitly honoring the curve's Act365F axis does not change these recorded values. Re-blessed 2026-07-22: discount_margin sign-convention fix from the 2026-07-21 fixed-income audit (commit c5c6a7a3d). The old solver added the trial DM to the loan's *coupon* spread and repriced on the unshifted discount curve, making PV increasing in DM, so the solved DM was approximately the negative of the true DM (old: -0.02870519217354197). The metric now follows the market-standard curve-DM convention (Fabozzi; Bloomberg YAS): cashflows stay projected at the contractual 375bp margin and the DM is added to the periodically-compounded zero rate of the discount curve via the shared z_spread_discount_factor mechanics, identical to the FRN DM path. PV is strictly decreasing in DM. New: discount_margin=0.029426445475274027 (+294bp over USD-CORP; below the 375bp contractual margin because USD-CORP already embeds corporate spread over the SOFR projection curve, and positive because the model PV sits above the 99.0 quoted-clean-price dirty target). Only this metric moved; npv/ytm/dv01/cs01 are unchanged, confirming the base pricing flows were untouched. Re-blessed 2026-09-07: discounting DV01 and CS01 now run through the quote-risk view (`term_loan::metrics::risk_view`). The quoted clean price 99.0 is converted to a z-spread once and held while UnifiedDv01 applies the parallel rate shock and ZSpreadParallelCs01 applies the +/-1bp z-spread bump on that quote-reproducing book. NPV, YTM, and discount margin stay on the unpinned model price and were not retargeted. Old: dv01=-1113.0240003746, cs01=-8120.933197071776. New: dv01=-524.3815551586449, cs01=-9253.50447811. Re-baselined 2026-09-18 after commit 413953021's cashflow-accrual and sensitivity changes; drift is at the 1e-4 relative level. Re-blessed 2026-09-23: the term-loan instrument PV is now anchored at the valuation date like the bond and the revolver (settlement-date model value x DF(as_of, settlement) plus any flows paid before settlement; here none), instead of reporting the settlement-date value. Old npv=27324079.449001934, new npv=27309017.1409: the ratio 0.99944875 is DF(2026-04-30 -> settlement) on USD-CORP (about 5% over 4 days). dv01 moves from -524.0696116890758 to -550.912787197 because the parallel shock now also discounts over the settlement lag (about -PV x 4/365 x 1bp = -30). Quote-space metrics (discount_margin, ytm, cs01) are unchanged.

npv.tolerance_reason: Self-test fixture: tolerance pinned to ~10x the worst observed deterministic FP residual on Finstack Quant's own calibrate + price round-trip (synthetic two-step calibration with USD-OIS + USD-SOFR-3M). Tightening to 1e-9 catches drift from refactors, FP-contract changes, calibration convention shifts, or pricing-kernel algorithm swaps that would be invisible at looser bands.

cs01.tolerance_reason: Self-test fixture: tolerance pinned to ~10x the worst observed deterministic FP residual on Finstack Quant's own calibrate + price round-trip. CS01 is the market-standard z-spread bump (the term-loan discounting pricer never consumes the hazard curve, so a par-spread/hazard bump leaves PV unchanged): the z-spread is solved to the quoted clean price (99.0% of notional), then bumped +/-1bp with a symmetric central difference. The Brent z-solve converges to 1e-10 on the spread axis and CS01's dependence on the anchor is second-order, so the value is deterministic to well within 1e-9; this band catches drift from refactors, FP-contract changes, or pricing-kernel algorithm swaps.
